relations.subject: monitoring:cbstats-histogram
relations.object: measures only front-end-thread time, not time spent fetching from disk
relations.evidence: This only measures the time spent in the front-end thread for each operation, meaning that the timings may not be representative if items have to be fetched from disk as part of the operation.

notable_absence.finding: The page names over 30 distinct timing categories (bg_load, disk_commit, sync_write_commit_majority, persistence_cursor_get_all_items, etc.) entirely at the ep-engine storage/replication-internals level. None of these appear anywhere else in the reused-namespace excerpt (monitoring:, log:). Per the round's mechanical warning, these are left as evidence/prose inside monitoring:cbstats-histogram rather than minted individually - this is the table-shaped-dump trap this round explicitly calls out.

cross_component_finding: The two sync_write_commit_* timing categories (sync_write_commit_majority, sync_write_commit_majority_and_persist_on_master, sync_write_commit_persist_to_majority) name durability levels by their internal replication/persistence mechanics rather than by the durability-level vocabulary used elsewhere in the docs - same underlying durability concept, described from the storage-engine's internal-timing perspective rather than the user-facing configuration perspective, with no page connecting the two vocabularies.
cross_product_finding: None - this page is Couchbase Server CLI-only with no Capella-facing surface.
